title.zh: 卷七十 唐書46: 列傳22 元行欽 夏魯奇 姚洪 李嚴 李仁矩 康思立 張敬達
title.en: Volume 70 Book of Later Tang 46: Biographies 22 - Yuan Xingqin, Xia Luqi, Yao Hong, Li Yan, Li Renju, Kang Sili, Zhang Jingda
title.raw: 卷七十 唐書46: 列傳22 元行欽 夏魯奇 姚洪 李嚴 李仁矩 康思立 張敬達 Volume 70 Book of Later Tang 46: Biographies 22 - Yuan Xingqin, Xia Luqi, Yao Hong, Li Yan, Li Renju, Kang Sili, Zhang Jingda

sentences.zh: 元行欽，本幽州劉守光之愛將。

translations.literal: Yuan Xingqin was originally a favorite commander of Liu Shouguang of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xingqin had begun as a favorite commander of Liu Shouguang of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 守光之奪父位也，令行欽攻大恩山，又令殺諸兄弟。

translations.literal: When Shouguang seized his father's position, he ordered Xingqin to attack Da'en Mountain and also ordered him to kill his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouguang seized his father's throne, he sent Xingqin against Da'en Mountain and ordered him to kill his brothers as well.

sentences.zh: 天祐九年，周德威攻圍山州，守光困蹙，令行欽於山北募兵，以應契丹。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianyou, Zhou Dewei besieged Shanzhou; Shouguang was hard pressed and ordered Xingqin to recruit troops north of the mountains to cooperate with the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Tianyou, Zhou Dewei besieged Shanzhou. Shouguang, cornered, ordered Xingqin to raise troops north of the mountains to link up with the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 時明宗為將，攻行欽於山北，與之接戰，矢及明宗馬鞍，既而以勢迫來降。

translations.literal: At that time Mingzong was a general; he attacked Xingqin north of the mountains and joined battle with him; an arrow reached Mingzong's saddle; afterward, pressed by circumstances, [Xingqin] came over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong was then a field commander. He attacked Xingqin in the northern hills, and in the fighting an arrow struck Mingzong's saddle. Soon afterward, hard pressed, Xingqin surrendered.

sentences.zh: 明宗憐其有勇，奏隸為假子，後因從征討，恩禮特隆。

translations.literal: Mingzong pitied him for his bravery, memorialized to have him enrolled as an adoptive son, and later, because he followed on campaigns, favored him with exceptional courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong admired his courage and had him registered as an adopted son. Thereafter, on campaign after campaign, he was treated with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 常臨敵擒生，必有所獲，名聞軍中。

translations.literal: Whenever he faced the enemy and took prisoners alive, he always gained something; his name was known throughout the army.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he met the enemy he took prisoners, and he always came away with something to show for it; his reputation spread through the army.

sentences.zh: 莊宗東定趙、魏，選驍健置之麾下，因索行欽，莊宗不得已而遣之。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong secured Zhao and Wei in the east, he selected the bravest and placed them under his command; he thus demanded Xingqin, and Zhuangzong, having no choice, sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong pacified Zhao and Wei in the east, he picked out the fiercest fighters for his personal command and asked for Xingqin. Zhuangzong, unable to refuse, sent him on.

sentences.zh: 時有散指揮都頭，名為散員，命行欽為都部署，賜姓，名紹榮。

translations.literal: At the time there were scattered command heads of the guard called "scattered guards"; he appointed Xingqin overall commander, granted him a surname, and named him Shaorong.
translations.idiomatic: There was then a corps of scattered guard commanders called the "scattered guards." Zhuangzong made Xingqin their overall commander, granted him the imperial surname, and gave him the name Shaorong.

sentences.zh: 莊宗好戰，勇於大敵，或臨陣有急兵，行欽必橫身解鬥翼衛之。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong loved battle and was bold before great enemies; whenever on the field there was an emergency, Xingqin always threw himself across [Zhuangzong] to break the fight and shield him on the wings.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong loved combat and was fearless before strong foes. Whenever danger closed in on the field, Xingqin would throw himself into the melee and fight at Zhuangzong's side to cover him.

sentences.zh: 莊宗營於德勝也，與汴軍戰於潘張，王師不利，諸軍奔亂。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong encamped at Desheng and fought the Bian army at Panzhang, the imperial army fared badly and the forces fled in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhuangzong was encamped at Desheng, he fought the Bian army at Panzhang. The imperial forces were beaten and the ranks broke in flight.

sentences.zh: 莊宗得三四騎而旋，中野為汴軍數百騎攢槊攻之，事將不測，行欽識其幟，急馳一騎，奮劍斷二矛，斬一級，汴軍乃解圍，翼莊宗還宮。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong escaped with only three or four horsemen; in open country several hundred Bian horsemen closed in with spears; the situation was dire; Xingqin recognized their banners, galloped forward alone, swung his sword and cut two spears, beheaded one man; the Bian army then broke the encirclement and escorted Zhuangzong back to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong got away with only three or four riders. In the open field several hundred Bian horsemen closed on him with leveled spears, and the outcome hung by a thread. Xingqin recognized their banners, spurred forward alone, slashed two spears apart with his sword, and cut down one man. The Bian troops broke off, and he escorted Zhuangzong back to camp.

sentences.zh: 莊宗因流涕言曰：「富貴與卿共之。」

translations.literal: Zhuangzong wept and said: "Wealth and honor shall be yours as well as mine."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong wept and said, "Whatever wealth and rank are mine shall be yours as well."

sentences.zh: 自是寵冠諸將，官至檢校太傅、忻州刺史。

translations.literal: From then on his favor surpassed all generals; he reached the posts of Grand Guardian in Examinership and prefect of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: From that day his favor outstripped every other general's, and he rose to Grand Guardian in Examinership and prefect of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗平梁，授武寧軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Liang, he was appointed military governor of Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong conquered Liang, he was made military governor of Wuning.

sentences.zh: 嘗因內宴群臣，使相預會，行欽官為保傅，當地褥下坐。

translations.literal: Once at an inner banquet for ministers, commissioners were also invited; Xingqin's post was guardian-tutor and he should sit below the floor cushions.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhuangzong gave an inner banquet for his ministers and invited the commissioners as well. Xingqin held the post of guardian-tutor and was to sit below the floor cushions.

sentences.zh: 酒酣樂作，莊宗敘生平戰陣之事，因左右顧視，曰：「紹榮安在？」

translations.literal: When the wine was warm and music played, Zhuangzong recounted battles of his life and looked about, saying: "Where is Shaorong?"
translations.idiomatic: As the wine warmed and the music began, Zhuangzong recounted the battles of his life, then glanced about and asked, "Where is Shaorong?"

sentences.zh: 所司奏云：「有敕，使相預會，紹榮散官，殿上無位。」

translations.literal: The department reported: "By imperial order, commissioners are invited to attend; Shaorong holds a scattered rank and has no seat in the hall."
translations.idiomatic: The master of ceremonies replied, "By imperial order the commissioners were invited to this gathering. Shaorong holds a scattered rank and has no place on the dais."

sentences.zh: 莊宗徹會不懌。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong dissolved the banquet displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong broke up the banquet in displeasure.

sentences.zh: 翌日，以行欽為同平章事，由是不宴百官於內殿，但宴武臣而已，

translations.literal: The next day he made Xingqin Chief Minister; henceforth he no longer feasted all officials in the inner hall but only military men,
translations.idiomatic: The next day he made Xingqin Chief Minister. After that he no longer entertained all the civil officials in the inner hall, but only his military commanders,

sentences.zh: 三年，行欽喪婦。

translations.literal: In the third year Xingqin mourned his wife.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Xingqin lost his wife.

sentences.zh: 莊宗有所愛宮人生皇子者，劉皇后心忌之，會行欽入侍，莊宗勞之曰：「紹榮喪婦復娶耶！

translations.literal: Zhuangzong had a palace lady he favored who had borne a prince; Empress Liu envied her; when Xingqin came to attend, Zhuangzong comforted him: "Shaorong, your wife has died—will you marry again?
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong favored a palace woman who had borne him a son, and Empress Liu resented her. When Xingqin came to attend him, Zhuangzong said kindly, "Shaorong, your wife is dead—will you take another?

sentences.zh: 吾給爾婚財。」

translations.literal: I will provide your marriage gifts."
translations.idiomatic: I will supply your wedding gifts."

sentences.zh: 皇后指所忌宮人謂莊宗曰：「皇帝憐紹榮，可使為婦。」

translations.literal: The empress pointed to the lady she envied and said to Zhuangzong: "The Emperor pities Shaorong—she may be made his wife."
translations.idiomatic: The empress pointed at the woman she hated and told Zhuangzong, "Your Majesty pities Shaorong—let her become his wife."

sentences.zh: 莊宗難違所請，微許之。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong found it hard to refuse the request and faintly assented.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong could not easily refuse and gave a faint assent.

sentences.zh: 皇后即命紹榮謝之，未退，肩輿已出。

translations.literal: The empress immediately ordered Shaorong to thank her; before he had withdrawn, a palanquin was already departing.
translations.idiomatic: The empress at once ordered Shaorong to thank her. Before he had even stepped back, a palanquin was already on its way out.

sentences.zh: 莊宗心不懌，佯不豫者累日，業已遣去，無如之何。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was displeased at heart; for many days he feigned indisposition; [she] had already been sent away, and there was nothing he could do.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was inwardly displeased and for days pretended to be unwell. The woman had already been sent off, and he could do nothing about it.

sentences.zh: 及貝州軍亂，趙在禮入魏州，莊宗方擇將，皇后曰：「小事不勞大將，促紹榮指揮可也。」

translations.literal: When the Beizhou army mutinied and Zhao Zaili entered Weizhou, Zhuangzong was selecting a general; the empress said: "For a small matter there is no need to trouble a great general; urging Shaorong to take command will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: When the Beizhou garrison mutinied and Zhao Zaili seized Weizhou, Zhuangzong was choosing a commander. The empress said, "A trifle like this need not burden a senior general—send Shaorong to take charge and that will do."

sentences.zh: 乃以行欽為鄴都行營招撫使，領騎二千進討。

translations.literal: He then made Xingqin pacification commissioner of the Ye capital field headquarters, leading two thousand horsemen to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: Xingqin was appointed pacification commissioner of the Ye capital field headquarters and led two thousand cavalry forward to attack.

sentences.zh: 洎至鄴城，攻之不能下，退保於澶州。

translations.literal: When he reached Yecheng he could not take it by assault and withdrew to hold Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Yecheng but could not capture it and fell back to defend Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，諸道之師稍集，復進軍於鄴城之南。

translations.literal: Before long the armies of the various circuits gradually gathered, and he again advanced south of Yecheng.
translations.idiomatic: Before long troops from the various circuits began to assemble, and he advanced again to the south of Yecheng.

sentences.zh: 及明宗為帥，領軍至鄴，行欽來謁於軍中，拜起之際，誤呼萬歲者再，明宗驚駭，遏之方止。

translations.literal: When Mingzong became commander and led troops to Ye, Xingqin came to pay his respects in camp; as he rose from his bow he twice cried "Long live [the Emperor]!" by mistake; Mingzong was startled and checked him before he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took command and marched to Ye, Xingqin came to pay his respects in camp. As he straightened from his bow he twice shouted "Long live the Emperor!" by mistake. Mingzong was alarmed and silenced him before he could go on.

sentences.zh: 既而明宗營於城西，行欽營於城南。

translations.literal: Mingzong then encamped west of the city and Xingqin encamped south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong then pitched camp west of the city and Xingqin south of it.

sentences.zh: 三月八日夜，明宗為亂軍所迫，惟行欽之軍不動，按甲以自固。

translations.literal: On the night of the eighth day of the third month Mingzong was pressed by the mutinous troops; only Xingqin's army did not move, holding their armor to secure themselves.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the eighth day of the third month the mutineers closed in on Mingzong. Only Xingqin's troops held their ground, keeping their armor on and standing firm.

sentences.zh: 明宗密令張虔釗至行欽營，戒之曰：「且堅壁勿動，計會同殺亂軍，莫錯疑誤。」

translations.literal: Mingzong secretly ordered Zhang Qianzhao to go to Xingqin's camp and warn him: "For now hold the walls and do not move; we plan to join in killing the mutinous troops—do not mistakenly suspect [us]."
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong secretly sent Zhang Qianzhao to Xingqin's camp with this warning: "Hold your position and do not move yet. We mean to strike the mutineers together—do not misread this and turn on us."

sentences.zh: 行欽不聽，將步騎萬人棄甲而退。

translations.literal: Xingqin would not listen and led ten thousand infantry and cavalry, casting off their armor, in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Xingqin refused to listen and withdrew with ten thousand foot and horse, throwing off their armor as they went.

sentences.zh: 自知失策，且保衛州，因誣奏明宗曰：「鎮師已入賊軍，終不為國使。」

translations.literal: Knowing he had erred in strategy, he held Weizhou for the time being and falsely memorialized against Mingzong, saying: "The circuit commander has already entered the rebel army and will never act for the state."
translations.idiomatic: Realizing he had blundered, he held Weizhou for the moment and sent a false report accusing Mingzong: "The frontier commander has gone over to the rebels and will never serve the dynasty again."

sentences.zh: 明宗既劫出鄴城，令人走馬上章，申理其事，言：「臣且於近郡聽進止。」

translations.literal: After Mingzong had been forced out of Yecheng, he sent a rider with a memorial to set forth the matter, saying: "Your servant will for the time being await instructions at a nearby prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: Once Mingzong had been carried off from Yecheng, he dispatched a mounted courier with a memorial to explain what had happened, saying, "Your servant will wait in a nearby prefecture for further orders."

sentences.zh: 莊宗覽奏釋然曰：「吾知紹榮妄矣。」

translations.literal: Zhuangzong read the memorial and said with relief: "I know Shaorong's report was false."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong read the memorial and said with relief, "I knew Shaorong was lying."

sentences.zh: 因令白從訓與明宗子繼璟至軍前，欲令見明宗，行欽縶繼璟於路。

translations.literal: He then ordered Bai Congxun and Mingzong's son Jijing to go to the front so that they might see Mingzong; Xingqin seized Jijing on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Bai Congxun and Mingzong's son Jijing to the front so they could meet Mingzong, but Xingqin seized Jijing on the way.

sentences.zh: 明宗凡奏軍機，拘留不達，故旬日之間，音驛斷絕。

translations.literal: All of Mingzong's military memorials were detained and not delivered; thus within ten days communications were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Every military report Mingzong sent was held up and never delivered, and within ten days all word from him had ceased.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗出成皋，知明宗在黎陽，復令繼璟渡河召明宗，行欽即殺之，仍勸班師。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong marched out from Chenggao and learned Mingzong was at Liyang, he again ordered Jijing to cross the river to summon Mingzong; Xingqin at once killed him and still urged withdrawal of the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong advanced from Chenggao and learned that Mingzong was at Liyang, he again ordered Jijing to cross the river and summon him. Xingqin killed Jijing on the spot and pressed for a general withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 四月一日，莊宗既崩，行欽引皇后、存渥，得七百騎出師子門，將之河中就存霸，沿路部下解散，從者數騎而已。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fourth month Zhuangzong died; Xingqin led the empress and Cunwo with seven hundred horsemen out the Lion Gate, intending to go to Hezhong to join Cunba; along the way his followers dispersed, and only a few horsemen remained.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fourth month Zhuangzong died. Xingqin escorted the empress and Cunwo with seven hundred horsemen out the Lion Gate, planning to reach Hezhong and join Cunba. Along the road his men melted away until only a handful of riders were left.

sentences.zh: 四日，至平陸縣界，為百姓所擒，縣令裴進折其足，檻車以獻。

translations.literal: On the fourth day he reached the border of Pinglu County, was seized by the common people, and Prefect Pei Jin broke his legs and sent him in a caged cart as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day he reached Pinglu County, where the local people seized him. Magistrate Pei Jin broke his legs and sent him to the capital in a cage cart.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，詔削奪行欽在位官爵，斬於洛陽。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he ordered that Xingqin's offices and ranks be stripped and had him executed at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Mingzong took the throne, an edict stripped Xingqin of every office and title he had held, and he was beheaded at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 夏魯奇，字邦傑，青州人也。

translations.literal: Xia Luqi, styled Bangjie, was a man of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Luqi, courtesy name Bangjie, was a native of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 初事宣武軍為軍校，與主將不協，遂歸於莊宗，以為護衛指揮使。

translations.literal: At first he served the Xuanwu army as a military officer; he did not get along with his commander and therefore went over to Zhuangzong, who made him commander of the guard.
translations.idiomatic: He first served the Xuanwu army as a regimental officer. At odds with his commander, he defected to Zhuangzong, who appointed him commander of the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 從周德威攻幽州，燕將有單廷珪、元行欽，時稱驍勇，魯奇與之鬥，兩不能解，將士皆釋兵縱觀。

translations.literal: Following Zhou Dewei in the attack on Youzhou, the Yan generals Shan Tinggui and Yuan Xingqin were then famed for fierceness; Luqi fought them and neither could overcome the other; officers and men all laid down their weapons to watch.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou Dewei he attacked Youzhou. The Yan generals Shan Tinggui and Yuan Xingqin were then renowned for valor. Luqi fought them to a standstill, and soldiers on both sides set down their weapons to watch.

sentences.zh: 幽州平，魯奇功居多。

translations.literal: When Youzhou was pacified, Luqi's merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhou fell, Luqi's contribution was the greatest of all.

sentences.zh: 梁將劉鄩在洹水，莊宗深入致師，鄩設伏於魏縣西南葭蘆中。

translations.literal: The Liang general Liu Yun was at Huanshui; Zhuangzong advanced deep to offer battle; Yun set an ambush in the reed marshes southwest of Wei County.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang general Liu Yun held Huanshui. Zhuangzong pushed deep to bring him to battle, and Yun laid an ambush in the reed beds southwest of Wei County.

sentences.zh: 莊宗不滿千騎，汴人伏兵萬餘，大噪而起，圍莊宗數重。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong had fewer than a thousand horsemen; the Bian men had more than ten thousand ambush troops, who rose with a great clamor and surrounded Zhuangzong in several rings.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong had fewer than a thousand horsemen with him. More than ten thousand Bian troops in ambush rose with a deafening roar and closed around him in ring after ring.

sentences.zh: 魯奇與王門關、烏德兒等奮命決戰，自午至申，俄而李存審兵至方解。

translations.literal: Luqi, Wang Menguan, Wude'er and others fought desperately from noon to the shen hour; presently Li Cunshen's troops arrived and the siege was broken.
translations.idiomatic: Luqi, Wang Menguan, Wude'er, and others fought for their lives from noon until mid-afternoon. Li Cunshen's troops arrived soon afterward and the encirclement was broken.

sentences.zh: 魯奇持槍攜劍，獨衛莊宗，手殺百餘人。

translations.literal: Luqi bore spear and sword and alone guarded Zhuangzong, killing more than a hundred men with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: Spear in one hand and sword in the other, Luqi alone shielded Zhuangzong and killed more than a hundred men himself.

sentences.zh: 烏德兒等被擒，魯奇傷痍遍體，自是莊宗尤憐之，曆磁州刺史。

translations.literal: Wude'er and others were captured; Luqi was wounded all over; from then on Zhuangzong pitied him especially and he served as prefect of Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wude'er and the others were taken prisoner. Luqi was covered with wounds, and from then on Zhuangzong favored him all the more. He later served as prefect of Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 中都之戰，汴人大敗，魯奇見王彥章，識之，單馬追及，槍擬其頸；

translations.literal: At the battle of Zhongdu the Bian forces were utterly defeated; Luqi saw Wang Yanzhang, recognized him, chased him alone on horseback and pressed a spear to his neck;
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Zhongdu the Bian army was routed. Luqi spotted Wang Yanzhang, recognized him, rode after him alone, and set a spear against his neck;

sentences.zh: 彥章顧曰：「爾非餘故人乎？」

translations.literal: Yanzhang looked back and said: "Are you not my old friend Yu?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang looked back and said, "Aren't you my old friend Yu?"

sentences.zh: 即擒之以獻。

translations.literal: He at once seized him and presented him [as a captive].
translations.idiomatic: He seized him on the spot and brought him in as his prize.

sentences.zh: 莊宗壯之，賞絹千匹。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong admired this and rewarded him with a thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was impressed and rewarded him with a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·趙庭隱傳》：王彥章守中都，庭隱在其軍中。

translations.literal: (From the Biography of Zhao Tingyin in the Jiuguo Zhi: Wang Yanzhang held Zhongdu, and Tingyin was in his army.
translations.idiomatic: (From the Biography of Zhao Tingyin in the Jiuguo Zhi: Wang Yanzhang defended Zhongdu, and Tingyin served in his army.

sentences.zh: 及彥章敗，庭隱為莊宗所獲，將以就戮，大將夏魯奇奏曰：「此矬也，其材可用。」

translations.literal: When Yanzhang was defeated, Tingyin was captured by Zhuangzong and was about to be put to death; the great general Xia Luqi memorialized, saying: "This is a dwarf, but his talent can be used."
translations.idiomatic: When Yanzhang was defeated, Tingyin was taken by Zhuangzong and was about to be executed. The great general Xia Luqi memorialized, "He is a short man, but his abilities are worth keeping."

sentences.zh: 遂釋之。）〉

translations.literal: He was then released.)〉
translations.idiomatic: He was then released.)〉

sentences.zh: 梁平，授鄭州防禦使。

translations.literal: When Liang was pacified, he was appointed defender of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang was conquered, he was made defender of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，授河陽節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed military governor of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed military governor of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 天成初，移鎮許州，加同平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was transferred to govern Xuzhou and made Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tiancheng era he was transferred to Xuzhou as military governor and made Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 魯奇性忠義，尤通吏道，撫民有術。

translations.literal: Luqi was by nature loyal and righteous, especially versed in administrative ways, and skilled at comforting the people.
translations.idiomatic: Luqi was loyal and upright by nature, especially skilled in governance, and knew how to win the people's trust.

sentences.zh: 及移鎮許田，孟州之民，萬眾遮道，斷鐙臥轍，五日不發。

translations.literal: When he was transferred to govern Xutian, the people of Mengzhou, tens of thousands strong, blocked the road, broke stirrups and lay across the wheel tracks, and for five days he could not depart.
translations.idiomatic: When he was reassigned to Xutian, tens of thousands of people from Mengzhou blocked his road, broke his stirrups, and lay across his carriage wheels. For five days he could not move on.

sentences.zh: 父老詣闕請留，明宗令中使諭之，方得離州。

translations.literal: Elders went to the capital to ask that he be kept; Mingzong sent a palace envoy to explain, and only then could he leave the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Local elders went to court to ask that he be kept. Mingzong sent a palace envoy to reason with them, and only then was he able to leave the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明宗討荊南，魯奇為副招討使，頃之，移鎮遂州。

translations.literal: Mingzong campaigned against Jingnan; Luqi was deputy pacification commissioner; shortly afterward he was transferred to govern Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong campaigned against Jingnan, Luqi served as deputy pacification commissioner. Soon afterward he was transferred to Suizhou as military governor.

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·李仁罕傳》：夏魯奇稟朝廷之命，繕治甲兵，將圖蜀，孟知祥與董璋謀先取魯奇，令仁罕攻遂州。）〉

translations.literal: (From the Biography of Li Renhan in the Jiuguo Zhi: Xia Luqi received the court's orders, repaired armor and weapons, and planned to strike Shu; Meng Zhixiang and Dong Zhang plotted first to take Luqi and ordered Renhan to attack Suizhou.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (From the Biography of Li Renhan in the Jiuguo Zhi: Xia Luqi obeyed the court's orders, repaired arms and armor, and prepared to move against Shu. Meng Zhixiang and Dong Zhang plotted to strike him first and ordered Renhan to attack Suizhou.)〉

sentences.zh: 董璋之叛，與孟知祥攻遂州，援路斷絕，兵盡食窮，

translations.literal: When Dong Zhang rebelled, he and Meng Zhixiang attacked Suizhou; the relief routes were cut off; troops were exhausted and food was gone,
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhang rebelled, he and Meng Zhixiang besieged Suizhou. Relief routes were cut, the garrison was spent, and provisions ran out,

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·李肇傳》：蜀師圍夏魯奇於遂州，唐師來援，劍門不守，肇領兵赴普安以拒之，唐師不得進。）〉

translations.literal: (From the Biography of Li Zhao in the Jiuguo Zhi: Shu troops besieged Xia Luqi at Suizhou; Tang troops came to relieve him; Jianmen was not held; Zhao led troops to Pu'an to resist, and the Tang army could not advance.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (From the Biography of Li Zhao in the Jiuguo Zhi: Shu forces besieged Xia Luqi at Suizhou. Tang relief troops marched to his aid, but Jianmen was left undefended. Zhao led troops to Pu'an to block them, and the Tang army could not get through.)〉

sentences.zh: 魯奇自刎而卒，時年四十九。

translations.literal: Luqi cut his own throat and died, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Luqi took his own life by cutting his throat. He was forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 帝聞其死也，慟哭之，厚給其家，贈太師、齊國公。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of his death he wept bitterly, richly provided for his family, and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Preceptor and Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor heard of his death he wept aloud, gave his family a generous settlement, and posthumously honored him as Grand Preceptor and Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 姚洪，本梁之小校也。

translations.literal: Yao Hong had originally been a petty officer of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong had begun as a junior officer in the service of Liang.

sentences.zh: 在梁時，經事董璋，長興初，率兵千人戍閬州。

translations.literal: While with Liang he had served Dong Zhang; at the beginning of Changxing he led a thousand troops to garrison Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: While still with Liang he had served under Dong Zhang. At the start of the Changxing era he led a thousand men to garrison Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 璋叛，領眾攻閬州，璋密令人誘洪，洪以大義拒之。

translations.literal: When Zhang rebelled he led his forces to attack Langzhou; Zhang secretly sent men to entice Hong, but Hong refused on grounds of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang rebelled he marched on Langzhou. Zhang secretly sent agents to win Hong over, but Hong refused on grounds of loyalty and duty.

sentences.zh: 及璋攻城，洪悉力拒守者三日，禦備既竭，城陷被擒。

translations.literal: When Zhang besieged the city, Hong resisted with all his strength for three days; when defenses were exhausted the city fell and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang laid siege to the city, Hong defended it with everything he had for three days. When his supplies and defenses were spent the city fell and he was taken.

sentences.zh: 璋謂洪曰：「爾頃為健兒，由吾獎拔至此；

translations.literal: Zhang said to Hong: "You were not long ago a stalwart warrior whom I promoted and raised to this position;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang said to Hong, "Only recently you were a common fighting man whom I promoted and raised to where you stand now.

sentences.zh: 吾書誘諭，投之於側，何相負耶？」

translations.literal: I sent you letters of enticement and placed them at your side—why have you betrayed me?"
translations.idiomatic: I wrote to persuade you and had the letters delivered to you—how can you turn against me?"

sentences.zh: 洪大罵曰：「老賊，爾為天子鎮帥，何苦反耶！

translations.literal: Hong cursed loudly: "Old bandit, you are a regional commander appointed by the Son of Heaven—why suffer yourself to rebel!
translations.idiomatic: Hong shouted back, "You old traitor! The Son of Heaven made you a frontier commander—why must you rebel!

sentences.zh: 爾既辜恩背主，吾與爾何恩，而雲相負！

translations.literal: You have already been ungrateful and betrayed your lord—what kindness is there between you and me, that you speak of betrayal!
translations.idiomatic: You have already betrayed your sovereign's grace—what debt do I owe you, that you accuse me of betrayal!

sentences.zh: 爾為李七郎奴，掃馬糞，得一臠殘炙，感恩無盡。

translations.literal: You were a slave of Li the Seventh, sweeping horse dung; you got a scrap of leftover roast and your gratitude was endless.
translations.idiomatic: You were Li the Seventh's slave, mucking out stables. You got a scrap of leftover meat and thought your debt of gratitude could never be repaid.

sentences.zh: 今明天子付與茅土，貴為諸侯，而驅徒結黨，圖為反噬。

translations.literal: Now the enlightened Son of Heaven has granted you a fief and made you a feudal lord among the nobles, yet you drive servants and form factions, plotting to turn and bite [your master].
translations.idiomatic: Now the enlightened Son of Heaven has given you a fief and raised you among the feudal lords, yet you herd servants into factions and plot to turn and bite the hand that fed you.

sentences.zh: 爾本奴才，則無恥；

translations.literal: You were born a slave and are without shame;
translations.idiomatic: You were born a slave and know no shame.

sentences.zh: 吾忠義之士，不忍為也。

translations.literal: I am a man of loyalty and righteousness and cannot bear to do such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: I am a man of loyalty and righteousness, and I cannot bring myself to do that.

sentences.zh: 吾可為天子死，不能與人奴苟生！」

translations.literal: I can die for the Son of Heaven—I cannot live on in servile submission to another man's slave!"
translations.idiomatic: I can die for the Son of Heaven, but I will not live on as the lackey of another man's slave!"

sentences.zh: 璋怒，令軍士十人，持刀刲割其膚，燃鑊於前，自取啖食，洪至死大罵不已。

translations.literal: Zhang in rage ordered ten soldiers with knives to flay his flesh, set a cauldron burning before him, and eat the pieces themselves; Hong cursed without cease until he died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang in fury ordered ten soldiers with knives to slice flesh from his body, set a cauldron blazing before him, and eat the pieces themselves. Hong cursed him without stopping until he died.

sentences.zh: 明宗聞之泣下，置洪二子於近衛，給賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Mingzong wept when he heard of it, placed Hong's two sons in the close guard, and gave them rich rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong heard of it he wept and placed Hong's two sons in the inner guard, granting them generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 李嚴，幽州人，本名讓坤。

translations.literal: Li Yan was a man of Youzhou; his original name was Rangkun.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan was a native of Youzhou; his birth name was Rangkun.

sentences.zh: 初仕燕，為刺史，涉獵書傳，便弓馬，有口辯，多遊藝，以功名自許。

translations.literal: At first he served Yan as a prefect; he read widely in books and histories, was skilled in archery and horsemanship, had a ready tongue, enjoyed many pastimes, and aspired to merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Yan as a prefect, read widely in the classics, was adept at archery and horsemanship, had a ready tongue, delighted in many arts, and set his heart on achievement and renown.

sentences.zh: 同光中，為客省使。

translations.literal: During Tongguang he was commissioner of the Reception Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongguang era he served as commissioner of the Reception Bureau.

sentences.zh: 奉使於蜀，及與王衍相見，陳使者之禮，因於笏記中具述莊宗興復之功，其警句云：「才過汶水，縛王彥章於馬前；

translations.literal: Sent as envoy to Shu, when he met Wang Yan he performed the ambassador's rites and in his tablet notes set forth Zhuangzong's achievements in restoration; a striking line ran: "Barely past the Wen River, Wang Yanzhang was bound before his horse;
translations.idiomatic: Sent on embassy to Shu, he met Wang Yan and performed the rites due an envoy. In the notes on his tablet he recounted Zhuangzong's deeds of restoration, with this striking line: "Hardly past the Wen River, Wang Yanzhang was bound before his horse;

sentences.zh: 旋及夷門，斬朱友貞於樓上。」

translations.literal: and soon at the Yimen Gate Zhu Youzhen was beheaded on the tower."
translations.idiomatic: and soon at the Yimen Gate Zhu Youzhen was beheaded on the tower."

sentences.zh: 嚴復聲韻清亮，蜀人聽之愕然。

translations.literal: Yan repeated this in a clear, resonant voice; the men of Shu listened in astonishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yan recited it again in a clear, ringing voice, and the men of Shu listened in stunned silence.

sentences.zh: 時蜀偽樞密使宋光嗣召嚴曲宴，因以近事訊於嚴。

translations.literal: The Shu pretender's Bureau of Military Affairs chief Song Guangsi invited Yan to a private banquet and questioned him about recent events.
translations.idiomatic: Song Guangsi, the bogus Shu commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, invited Yan to a private banquet and questioned him about recent affairs.

sentences.zh: 嚴對曰：「吾皇前年四月即位於鄴宮，當月下鄆州。

translations.literal: Yan replied: "Our Emperor took the throne at the Ye palace in the fourth month of the year before last and that same month descended on Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied, "Our Emperor took the throne at the Ye palace in the fourth month of the year before last and that same month marched on Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 十月四日，親統萬騎破賊中都，乘勝鼓行，遂誅汴孽，偽梁尚有兵三十萬，謀臣猛將，解甲倒戈。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the tenth month he personally commanded ten thousand horsemen and smashed the rebels at Zhongdu; pressing the victory with drum and march, he then executed the Bian scourge; the false Liang still had three hundred thousand troops, but stratagem-makers and fierce generals laid down armor and turned their blades.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the tenth month he personally led ten thousand horsemen and crushed the rebels at Zhongdu. Drums rolling, he pressed the victory forward, executed the Bian scourge, and though the false Liang still had three hundred thousand men, its strategists and fierce generals stripped off their armor and turned their swords around.

sentences.zh: 西盡甘、涼，東漸海外，南逾閩、浙，北極幽陵。

translations.literal: In the west it reached Gan and Liang; in the east it extended to the outer sea; in the south it crossed Min and Zhe; in the north it reached Youling.
translations.idiomatic: In the west his realm reached Gan and Liang; in the east it stretched to the open sea; in the south it crossed Min and Zhe; in the north it ran to Youling.

sentences.zh: 牧伯侯王，稱藩不暇，家財入貢，府實上供。

translations.literal: Regional lords and marquises had no leisure to style themselves vassals; household wealth went as tribute and treasury stores as upland supply.
translations.idiomatic: Regional lords and feudal princes scarcely had time to call themselves vassals; they sent household wealth as tribute and emptied their treasuries for the court.

sentences.zh: 吳國本朝舊臣，岐下先皇元老，遣子入侍，述職稱藩。

translations.literal: Wu was an old subject of our dynasty; below Qi stood a senior of the former emperor; he sent sons to attend court and rendered duty as a vassal.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was a longtime subject of our house; below Qi stood an elder of the former emperor who sent his son to court and fulfilled vassal duties.

sentences.zh: 淮、海之君，卑辭厚貢，湖湘、荊楚，杭越、甌閩，異貨奇珍，府無虛月。

translations.literal: Lords of the Huai and the sea used humble words and rich tribute; from Hunan, Hubei, Hang-Yue, and Ou-Min came exotic goods and rare treasures, and the treasury had no empty month.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers of the Huai and coastal regions sent humble embassies and lavish gifts; from the lakes and rivers of Hunan and Hubei to Hangzhou, Yue, Wenzhou, and Fujian, exotic goods and rarities arrived so that the court storehouses knew no idle month.

sentences.zh: 吾皇以德懷來，以威款附。

translations.literal: Our Emperor with virtue embraces those who come and with might wins their attachment.
translations.idiomatic: Our Emperor wins men by virtue and binds them by power.

sentences.zh: 順則涵之以恩澤，逆則問之以干戈，四海車書，大同非晚。」

translations.literal: If they submit, he bathes them in grace; if they rebel, he questions them with arms; within the four seas chariots and writing unite, and great unity is not far off."
translations.idiomatic: The obedient he shelters in grace; the defiant he meets with arms. When chariots and writing unite the four seas, universal rule will come soon."

sentences.zh: 光嗣曰：「餘所未知，惟岐下宋公，我之姻好，洞見其心，反覆多端，專謀跋扈，大不足信也。

translations.literal: Guangsi said: "Of the rest I do not know; only Duke Song below Qi, my marriage kin—I see through his heart: shifting and many-sided, bent on overbearing ambition, wholly unworthy of trust.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi said, "I cannot speak for the rest, but Duke Song below Qi is my kinsman by marriage, and I know his heart. He is changeable and scheming, bent on domineering power, and is not to be trusted at all.

sentences.zh: 似聞契丹部族，近日稍強，大國可無慮乎？」

translations.literal: I seem to hear that the Khitan tribes have lately grown somewhat strong—can your great state be without concern?"
translations.idiomatic: I hear the Khitan tribes have grown stronger of late. Surely your great state has no cause for worry?"

sentences.zh: 嚴曰：「子言契丹之強盛，孰若偽梁？」

translations.literal: Yan said: "You speak of Khitan strength—compared with whom, the false Liang?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "You speak of Khitan might—compared with what? The false Liang?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「比梁差劣也。」

translations.literal: He said: "Compared with Liang they are rather inferior."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "They are somewhat weaker than Liang was."

sentences.zh: 嚴曰：「吾國視契丹如蚤虱耳，以其無害，不足爬搔。

translations.literal: Yan said: "Our state regards the Khitan as fleas and lice; because they do no harm, they are not worth scratching.
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "Our realm looks on the Khitan as fleas and lice. They do no harm, so they are not worth troubling over.

sentences.zh: 吾良將勁兵布天下，彼不勞一郡之兵，一校之眾，則懸首槀街，盡為奴擄。

translations.literal: Our good generals and strong soldiers are spread across the realm; they would need neither a single prefecture's troops nor a single command's men, and Khitan heads would hang at the drying rack, all taken as slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Our finest generals and strongest troops are posted across the empire. We would not need even one prefecture's force or one command's men to hang their heads at the execution ground and take them all as captives.

sentences.zh: 但以天生四夷，當置度外，不在九州之本，未欲窮兵黷武也。」

translations.literal: Only because the Four Barbarians are born by nature, they should be set beyond measure, outside the root of the Nine Provinces; we do not yet wish to exhaust the army in reckless war."
translations.idiomatic: Only because the barbarians of the four quarters are born beyond our realm, they should be left outside our concern, outside the heartland of the Nine Provinces. We have no wish yet to wear out the army in endless war."

sentences.zh: 光嗣聞辯對，畏而奇之。

translations.literal: Guangsi heard this eloquent reply and was both afraid and struck with wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi heard this sharp reply and was both afraid and astonished.

sentences.zh: 時王衍失政，嚴知其可取，使還具奏，故平蜀之謀，始於嚴。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Yan's government was failing; Yan knew Shu could be taken, had him return and report in full, and so the plan to pacify Shu began with Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan's rule was failing, and Yan saw that Shu could be taken. He sent him back to report in full, and thus the plan to conquer Shu began with Yan.

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜起軍之日，以嚴為三川招撫使，嚴與先鋒使康延孝將兵五千，先驅閣道，或馳以詞說，或威以兵鋒，大軍未及，所在降下。

translations.literal: On the day Guo Chongtao raised the army, Yan was made pacification commissioner of the Three Rivers; Yan and the vanguard commissioner Kang Yanxiao led five thousand troops, advancing first along the plank roads, sometimes galloping with words to persuade, sometimes threatening with the edge of arms; before the main army arrived, wherever they went submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Chongtao took the field, Yan was made pacification commissioner of the Three Rivers. Yan and the vanguard commander Kang Yanxiao led five thousand men ahead along the mountain roads, winning some places by persuasion and others by force. Before the main army arrived, city after city surrendered.

sentences.zh: 延孝在漢州，王衍與書曰：「 可請李司空先來，餘即舉城納款。」

translations.literal: Yanxiao was at Hanzhou; Wang Yan wrote to him, saying: " You may ask Minister Li to come first; I will then surrender the city."
translations.idiomatic: Yanxiao was at Hanzhou when Wang Yan wrote to him: "Please ask Minister Li to come first, and I will surrender the city at once."

sentences.zh: 眾咸以討蜀之謀始於嚴，衍以甘言，將誘而殺之，欲不令往。

translations.literal: All held that the plan to attack Shu had begun with Yan, that Yan's sweet words were meant to lure and kill him, and they wished not to let him go.
translations.idiomatic: The troops all said the Shu campaign had begun with Yan, that Wang Yan's flattering words were a trap to lure and kill him, and they wanted to keep him from going.

sentences.zh: 嚴聞之喜，即馳騎入益州，衍見嚴於母前，以母、妻為托。

translations.literal: Yan heard this with joy and at once galloped into Yizhou; Wang Yan received Yan before his mother and entrusted his mother and wife to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was delighted to hear it and rode at once into Yizhou. Wang Yan received him before his mother and entrusted his mother and wife to Yan's care.

sentences.zh: 即日，引蜀使歐陽彬迎謁魏王繼岌。

translations.literal: That same day he led the Shu envoy Ouyang Bin to welcome and pay court to Prince Jiji of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he brought the Shu envoy Ouyang Bin to pay homage to Prince Jiji of Wei.

sentences.zh: 蜀平班師，會明宗即位，遷泗州防禦使兼客省使。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified the army returned; it happened that Mingzong took the throne, and Yan was transferred to defender of Sizhou while retaining the post of commissioner of the Reception Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu was pacified the army withdrew. Mingzong then took the throne, and Yan was made defender of Sizhou while keeping his post as commissioner of the Reception Bureau.

sentences.zh: 長興初，安重誨謀欲控製兩川，嚴乃求為西川兵馬都監，庶效方略。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changxing, An Chonghui plotted to control the Two Chuan; Yan then asked to be military inspector of Xichuan, hoping to put his stratagems to use.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Changxing era, An Chonghui schemed to control the Two Chuan, and Yan asked to be made military inspector of Xichuan so he could put his plans into effect.

sentences.zh: 孟知祥覺之，既至，執而害之。

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang perceived this; once Yan arrived, he seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang saw through him, and when Yan arrived he seized and executed him.

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·王彥銖傳》：李嚴之為監軍也，密懷異謀，知祥數其過，命彥銖擒斬之，嚴之左右無敢動者。）〉

translations.literal: (From the Biography of Wang Yanyin in the Records of the Nine Kingdoms: When Li Yan served as military inspector, he secretly harbored a different design; Zhixiang counted his offenses and ordered Yanyin to seize and behead him, and none of Yan's attendants dared move.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (From the Biography of Wang Yanyin in the Records of the Nine Kingdoms: When Li Yan served as military inspector, he secretly plotted rebellion. Zhixiang listed his offenses and ordered Yanyin to seize and execute him, and none of Yan's attendants dared stir.)〉

sentences.zh: 贈太保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 嚴之母，賢明婦人。

translations.literal: Yan's mother was a wise and worthy woman.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's mother was a wise and virtuous woman.

sentences.zh: 初，嚴將赴蜀，母曰：「汝前啟破蜀之謀，今又入蜀，將死報蜀人矣！

translations.literal: At first, when Yan was about to go to Shu, his mother said: "You once opened the plan to destroy Shu; now you enter Shu again—you will die repaying the people of Shu!
translations.idiomatic: When Yan was about to depart for Shu, his mother said, "You first proposed the plan to destroy Shu, and now you enter Shu again. You will die repaying the people of Shu!

sentences.zh: 與汝永訣。」

translations.literal: I take my eternal leave of you."
translations.idiomatic: I bid you farewell forever."

sentences.zh: 既而果如其言。

translations.literal: In the end it came about exactly as she had said.
translations.idiomatic: In the end it happened exactly as she had foretold.

sentences.zh: 李仁矩，本明宗在藩鎮時客將也。

translations.literal: Li Renju had originally been a guest officer when Mingzong held a princely fief.
translations.idiomatic: Li Renju had originally been a guest officer in Mingzong's household when he held a princely fief.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，錄其趨走之勞，擢居內職，復為安重誨所庇，故數年之間，遷為客省使、左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he recorded Renju's labor in attendance and raised him to inner service; again he was sheltered by An Chonghui, and within a few years he was transferred to commissioner of the Reception Bureau and Grand General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne, he rewarded Renju for his years of service and promoted him to the inner court. Under An Chonghui's patronage he rose within a few years to commissioner of the Reception Bureau and Grand General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 天成中，因奉使東川，董璋張筵以召之，仁矩貪於館舍，與倡妓酣飲，日既中而不至，大為璋所詬辱，自是深銜之。

translations.literal: During Tiancheng, on a mission to Eastern Chuan, Dong Zhang spread a banquet to summon him; Renju lingered greedily at the lodge, drinking deep with singing girls; the sun had passed noon and he had not come, and Zhang greatly reviled and shamed him—from this he bore a deep grudge.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiancheng era, while on mission to Eastern Chuan, Dong Zhang held a banquet in his honor. Renju stayed at the lodge drinking with courtesans and did not arrive until after noon. Dong Zhang rebuked him harshly, and from that day Renju nursed a deep hatred.

sentences.zh: 長興初，璋既跋扈於東川，重誨奏以仁矩為閬州節度使，俾伺璋之反狀，時物議以為不可。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changxing, Zhang was already overbearing in Eastern Chuan; Chonghui memorialized making Renju military governor of Langzhou to spy on Zhang's signs of rebellion; at the time public opinion held this unwise.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Changxing era, Dong Zhang was already acting arrogantly in Eastern Chuan. Chonghui memorialized appointing Renju military governor of Langzhou to watch for signs of rebellion, though public opinion at the time held this unwise.

sentences.zh: 及仁矩至鎮，偵璋所為，曲形奏報，地裏遐僻，朝廷莫知事實，激成璋之逆節，由仁矩也。

translations.literal: When Renju reached his command, he spied on Zhang's actions and reported them in distorted form; the region was remote and secluded, and the court did not know the facts—Zhang's rebellious course was provoked by Renju.
translations.idiomatic: Once Renju reached his post, he spied on Dong Zhang and sent distorted reports to court. The region was remote, and Beijing knew nothing of the truth. Dong Zhang's rebellion was provoked by Renju.

sentences.zh: 長興元年冬十月，璋自率凶黨，以攻其城。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the first year of Changxing, Zhang personally led his villainous band to attack the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter in the first year of Changxing, Dong Zhang personally led his ruffians to attack the city.

sentences.zh: 仁矩召軍校謀守戰利害，皆曰：「璋久圖反計，以賂誘士心，凶氣方盛，未可與戰，宜堅壁以守之。

translations.literal: Renju summoned army officers to discuss the gains and losses of defense and battle; all said: "Zhang long plotted rebellion, using bribes to win soldiers' hearts; his vicious momentum is at its height—we cannot fight him yet and should hold the walls firm.
translations.idiomatic: Renju summoned his officers to discuss whether to defend or attack. They all said, "Dong Zhang has long plotted rebellion and has bought the soldiers' loyalty. His momentum is fierce. We should not fight yet but hold the walls firm.

sentences.zh: 儻旬浹之間，大軍東至，即賊必退。」

translations.literal: If within ten days the great army comes from the east, the bandits will surely withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days the main army will arrive from the east, and the rebels will surely retreat."

sentences.zh: 仁矩曰：「蜀兵懦，安能當我精甲！」

translations.literal: Renju said: "Shu soldiers are cowardly—how can they face our elite armor!"
translations.idiomatic: Renju said, "Shu troops are cowards. How can they stand against our elite armor!"

sentences.zh: 即驅之出戰，兵未交，為賊所敗。

translations.literal: He at once drove them out to battle; before the armies had clashed they were defeated by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He at once drove them out to fight. Before the lines met, they were routed by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 既而城陷，仁矩被擒，舉族為璋所害。

translations.literal: Soon the city fell; Renju was captured, and his whole clan was killed by Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the city fell. Renju was captured, and Dong Zhang killed his entire clan.

sentences.zh: 康思立，晉陽人也。

translations.literal: Kang Sili was a man of Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Sili was a native of Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 少善騎射，事武皇為爪牙，署河東親騎軍使。

translations.literal: In youth he excelled at mounted archery, served Emperor Wu as a claw-and-fang man, and was appointed commander of the Hedong Personal Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he excelled at mounted archery, served Emperor Wu as a trusted fighter, and was appointed commander of the Hedong Personal Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 莊宗嗣位，從解圍於上黨，敗梁人於柏鄉，及平薊兵，後戰於河上，皆有功，累承製加檢校戶部尚書，右突騎指揮使。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong succeeded, he followed in relieving the siege at Shangdang, defeated Liang men at Baixiang, pacified the Ji troops, and later fought on the Yellow River—all with merit; he was repeatedly appointed by edict as acting Minister of Revenue and commander of the Right Vanguard Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong succeeded, he helped lift the siege at Shangdang, defeated the Liang at Baixiang, pacified the Ji forces, and later fought along the Yellow River, winning merit in every campaign. He was repeatedly promoted by edict to acting Minister of Revenue and commander of the Right Vanguard Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位，繼改軍帥，賜忠勇拱衛功臣，加檢校尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he was again changed to army commander, granted the title of merit subject Loyal Brave Arch-guard, and made acting Vice Director of the Right Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he was again made an army commander, granted the title Loyal Brave Arch-guard Merit Subject, and promoted to acting Vice Director of the Right Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天成元年，授應州刺史，尋移嵐州，充北面諸蕃部族都監。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng he was appointed prefect of Yingzhou, soon moved to Lanzhou, and served as overall supervisor of the northern frontier tribal peoples.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiancheng he was made prefect of Yingzhou, soon transferred to Lanzhou, and appointed overall supervisor of the northern frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷宿州團練使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to training commissioner of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to training commissioner of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，領昭武軍節度、利巴集等州觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he led the Zhaowu army as military governor and commissioner for observation and disposition of Li, Ba, Ji, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made military governor of the Zhaowu army and commissioner for observation and disposition of Li, Ba, Ji, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 改賜耀忠保節功臣。

translations.literal: He was again granted the merit title Yao Loyalty Preserving Festival.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the new merit title Yao Loyalty Preserving Festival.

sentences.zh: 長興初，朝廷舉兵討東川董璋，詔監西面行營軍馬都指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changxing the court raised troops against Dong Zhang of Eastern Chuan and ordered him to supervise the western campaign army as overall horse commander.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Changxing era the court raised troops against Dong Zhang of Eastern Chuan and ordered him to supervise the western campaign as overall commander of the army's horse units.

sentences.zh: 二年，移鎮陝州。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to govern Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was transferred to govern Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：潞王至靈寶，思立謀固守陝城以俟康義誠。

translations.literal: (From the Comprehensive Mirror: When the Prince of Lu reached Lingbao, Sili planned to hold Shaan city firm and await Kang Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: (From the Comprehensive Mirror: When Prince Lu reached Lingbao, Sili planned to hold Shaan city and await Kang Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 先是，捧聖五百騎戍陝，為潞王前鋒，至城下，呼城上人曰：「禁軍十萬已奉新帝，爾輩數人奚為！

translations.literal: Earlier, five hundred Pingsheng horsemen garrisoned Shaan as the Prince of Lu's vanguard; reaching below the wall, they called to those above: "The imperial army of a hundred thousand has already honored the new emperor—what are you few men doing!
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, five hundred Pingsheng cavalry had garrisoned Shaan as the Prince of Lu's vanguard. Reaching the foot of the wall, they shouted up, "A hundred thousand men of the imperial guard have already acclaimed the new emperor. What are you few men still doing here!

sentences.zh: 徒累一城人塗地耳！」

translations.literal: You will only heap one city's people in blood on the ground!"
translations.idiomatic: You will only bring bloodshed on a whole city for nothing!"

sentences.zh: 於是捧聖卒爭出迎，思立不能禁，不得已，亦出迎。）〉

translations.literal: Then the Pingsheng soldiers vied to go out and welcome them; Sili could not forbid it and, having no choice, also went out to welcome them.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Then the Pingsheng troops rushed out to welcome them. Sili could not stop them and, with no choice left, went out to welcome them as well.)〉

sentences.zh: 清泰初，改授邢台，累官至檢校太傅，封會稽郡開國侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was reassigned to Xingtai, rose cumulatively to acting Grand Preceptor, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qingtai era he was reassigned to Xingtai, rose to acting Grand Preceptor, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 二年，入為右神武統軍。

translations.literal: In the second year he entered the capital as commander of the Right Divine Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he entered the capital as commander of the Right Divine Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 三年，充北面行營馬軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the third year he served as overall commander of the northern campaign's horse army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he served as overall commander of the horse units in the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 是歲閏十一月，卒於軍，年六十三。

translations.literal: That year, in the intercalary eleventh month, he died in the army at the age of sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: That year, in the intercalary eleventh month, he died in camp at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 張敬達，字志通，代州人，小字生鐵。

translations.literal: Zhang Jingda, style Zhigong, was a man of Daizhou; his childhood name was Raw Iron.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingda, courtesy name Zhigong, was a native of Daizhou; his childhood name was Raw Iron.

sentences.zh: 父審，素有勇，事武皇為列校，曆廳直軍使，同光初，卒於軍。

translations.literal: His father Shen had valor by nature, served Emperor Wu as a column commander, passed through the post of Hall Direct army commander, and in early Tongguang died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shen was brave by nature, served Emperor Wu as a column commander, rose to Hall Direct army commander, and died in service early in the Tongguang era.

sentences.zh: 敬達少以騎射著名，莊宗知之，召令繼父職；

translations.literal: Jingda in youth was famed for mounted archery; Zhuangzong knew of it and summoned him to inherit his father's post;
translations.idiomatic: Jingda was famed in youth for mounted archery. Zhuangzong knew of him and summoned him to inherit his father's post;

sentences.zh: 平河南有功，繼加檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: in pacifying Henan he had merit and was then made acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: he won merit pacifying Henan and was then made acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，曆捧聖指揮使、檢校尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he passed through commander of the Pingsheng guard and acting Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne, he served as commander of the Pingsheng guard and acting Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 長興中，改河東馬步軍都指揮使，超授檢校司徒，領欽州刺史。

translations.literal: During Changxing he was changed to overall commander of the Hedong horse and foot armies, superseded in appointment to acting Minister of Education, and led Qinzhou as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changxing era he was made overall commander of the Hedong horse and foot armies, promoted in one step to acting Minister of Education, and appointed prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，加檢校太保、應州節度使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made acting Grand Guardian and military governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made acting Grand Guardian and military governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷雲州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 時以契丹率族帳自黑榆林挎剌泊至沒越泊，雲借漢界水草，敬達每聚兵塞下，以遏其衝。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan led their clan tents from Heilinlin through Kulabo to Moyuebo; Yun borrowed Han border water and grass, and Jingda each time gathered troops below the pass to block their thrust.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Khitan led their clans from Heilinlin through Kulabo to Moyuebo, grazing on Han borderlands. Jingda repeatedly massed troops below the passes to block their advance.

sentences.zh: 契丹竟不敢南牧，邊人賴之。

translations.literal: The Khitan ultimately did not dare pasture south, and the border people relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ultimately did not dare drive their herds south, and the border people owed their safety to him.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，自彭門移鎮平陽，加檢校太傅，從石敬瑭為北面兵馬副總管，仍屯兵雁門。

translations.literal: During Qingtai he was moved from Pengmen to govern Pingyang, made acting Grand Preceptor, followed Shi Jingtang as deputy overall commander of the northern army and horse forces, and still garrisoned troops at Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingtai era he was transferred from Pengmen to Pingyang, made acting Grand Preceptor, and served under Shi Jingtang as deputy overall commander of the northern forces while keeping his troops at Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 未幾，晉高祖建義，末帝詔以敬達為北面行營都招討使，仍使悉引部下兵圍太原，以定州節度使楊光遠副焉。

translations.literal: Before long, when Jin Gaozu raised the righteous army, the Last Emperor edicted Jingda as overall pacification commissioner of the northern campaign and still had him lead all his subordinate troops to besiege Taiyuan, with Yang Guangyuan, military governor of Dingzhou, as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, when the Jin founder rose in revolt, the Last Emperor appointed Jingda overall pacification commissioner of the northern campaign and ordered him to lead all his troops to besiege Taiyuan, with Yang Guangyuan, military governor of Dingzhou, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 尋統兵三萬，營於晉安鄉。

translations.literal: Soon he commanded thirty thousand troops and encamped at Jin'an village.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he took command of thirty thousand men and encamped at Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 末帝自六月繼有詔促令攻取，敬達設長城連柵、雲梯飛炮，使工者運其巧思，窮土木之力。

translations.literal: From the sixth month the Last Emperor repeatedly issued edicts urging capture; Jingda set long walls and linked palisades, cloud ladders and flying cannon, had artisans apply their clever designs, and exhausted the power of earth and wood.
translations.idiomatic: From the sixth month onward the Last Emperor repeatedly ordered him to take the city. Jingda built long walls and linked palisades, cloud ladders and siege engines, set artisans to every device, and exhausted every effort of engineering.

sentences.zh: 時督事者每有所構，則暴風大雨，平地水深數尺，而城柵崩墮，竟不能合其圍。

translations.literal: Whenever those supervising the work set up something, violent wind and great rain followed; on level ground the water was several feet deep, city palisades collapsed and fell, and in the end they could not close the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the builders raised some new work, violent storms followed. Water on the plain stood several feet deep, walls and palisades collapsed, and in the end they could not close the siege ring.

sentences.zh: 九月，契丹至，敬達大敗，尋為所圍。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Khitan arrived; Jingda was greatly defeated and soon was besieged.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Khitan arrived. Jingda suffered a crushing defeat and was soon surrounded.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖及蕃眾自晉安寨南門外，長百餘里，闊五十里，布以氈帳，用毛索掛鈴，而部伍多犬，以備警急。

translations.literal: Jin Gaozu and the barbarian masses from outside the south gate of the Jin'an stockade stretched more than a hundred li in length and fifty li in breadth, spread with felt tents, using hair ropes hung with bells, and the units mostly had dogs to guard against sudden alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founder and the barbarian hosts spread from beyond the south gate of the Jin'an camp for more than a hundred li in length and fifty li across, pitching felt tents and hanging bells on hair ropes. Most units kept dogs to sound the alarm.

sentences.zh: 營中嘗有夜遁者，出則犬吠鈴動，跬步不能行焉。

translations.literal: In the camp there were once men who fled by night; when they went out the dogs barked and the bells moved, and they could not advance a half step.
translations.idiomatic: When men in the camp tried to flee by night, the dogs barked and the bells rang at the first step, and they could not move.

sentences.zh: 自是敬達與麾下部曲五萬人，馬萬匹，無由四奔，但見穹廬如崗阜相屬，諸軍相顧失色。

translations.literal: From this Jingda and the fifty thousand men and ten thousand horses under his command had no way to flee in the four directions; they only saw domed tents like hill ranges joined, and the armies looked at one another and lost color.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Jingda and his fifty thousand men and ten thousand horses had no escape in any direction. They saw only dome tents stretching like linked hills, and the armies looked at one another in dismay.

sentences.zh: 始則削木篩糞，以飼其馬，日望朝廷救軍，及漸羸死，則與將士分食之，馬盡食殫。

translations.literal: At first they shaved wood and sifted dung to feed their horses, daily hoping for the court's relief army; as the horses gradually weakened and died, they divided and ate them with the generals and soldiers until the horses were all eaten up.
translations.idiomatic: At first they shaved wood and sifted dung to feed the horses, daily hoping for relief from court. As the horses weakened and died, officers and men shared the meat until every horse was eaten.

sentences.zh: 副將楊光遠、次將安審琦知不濟，勸敬達宜早降以求自安。

translations.literal: The deputy Yang Guangyuan and the second commander An Shenqi knew the cause was lost and urged Jingda to surrender early to seek his own safety.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy Yang Guangyuan and the second-in-command An Shenqi saw that all was lost and urged Jingda to surrender early and save himself.

sentences.zh: 敬達曰：「吾受恩於明宗，位曆方鎮，主上授我大柄，而失律如此，已有愧於心也。

translations.literal: Jingda said: "I received grace from Mingzong, held posts across the regional commands, and the sovereign entrusted me with great authority—yet I have lost discipline like this and already have shame in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Jingda said, "I owe my rise to Mingzong. I have held regional command, and the sovereign entrusted me with great authority. To fail so badly already shames me to the heart.

sentences.zh: 今救軍在近，旦暮雪恥有期，諸公何相迫耶！

translations.literal: Now the relief army is near; dawn and dusk will bring a day to wipe away shame—why do you gentlemen press me so!
translations.idiomatic: Relief is near, and we may yet wipe away this shame. Why do you press me so!

sentences.zh: 待勢窮，則請殺吾，攜首以降，亦未為晚。」

translations.literal: Wait until the situation is exhausted, then ask to kill me and carry my head to surrender—it will not yet be too late."
translations.idiomatic: When all is truly lost, you may kill me and carry my head to surrender. That will not be too late."

sentences.zh: 光遠、審琦知敬達意未決，恐坐成魚肉，遂斬敬達以降。

translations.literal: Guangyuan and Shenqi knew Jingda's mind was not yet settled and feared sitting still would make them fish on the chopping block; they then beheaded Jingda and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan and Shenqi saw that Jingda had not made up his mind and feared that if they waited they would become helpless prey. They beheaded Jingda and surrendered.

sentences.zh: （《契丹國志》：楊光遠謀害張敬達，諸將高行周陰為之備，敬達疏於防禦，推遠行周等。

translations.literal: (From the Khitan State Annals: Yang Guangyuan plotted to harm Zhang Jingda; the generals Gao Xingzhou secretly prepared against it; Jingda was lax in defense and kept Gao Xingzhou and the others at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: (From the Khitan State Annals: Yang Guangyuan plotted to kill Zhang Jingda. General Gao Xingzhou secretly prepared against it, but Jingda was lax in his defenses and kept Gao Xingzhou and the others at a distance.

sentences.zh: 清晨，光遠上謁，見敬達左右無人，遂殺之。）〉

translations.literal: At early dawn Guangyuan went to an audience, saw no one at Jingda's side, and then killed him.)〉
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Guangyuan came to call on him, found no one at Jingda's side, and killed him.)〉
